key_idea: Every entrance on the border touches at most one interior cell, hence one connected region, so the answer is the number of regions containing a dot that touch an entrance, and unreachable dots are those in regions touching none.
sketch: Read the grid with getline because rows contain spaces (pad short rows in case trailing spaces were stripped). Flood fill the interior non-X cells (space or dot) into components, counting dots per component and marking a component as enterable if any of its cells is adjacent to a border letter A-W. Players = enterable components with at least one dot; unreachable = total dots in non-enterable components. Never walk through border cells, which enforces that adjacent doors do not connect, and X on the border is a wall, not an entrance. O(nm).
